text: The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.
location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: The less you know, the surer you feel. Real wisdom starts with knowing how little you know.

text: Men have died from time to time and worms have eaten them, but not for love.
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Heartbreak feels fatal and never is. People get over it.

text: Well, Time is the old justice that examines all such offenders, and let time try.
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Time tests everyone in the end. Let it sort out who is real.

text: Then to have seen much and to have nothing is to have rich eyes and poor hands.
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Experience without anything built from it is just sightseeing.

text: But O, how bitter a thing it is to look into happiness through another man’s eyes!
location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 2
plain: Watching someone else get what you want hurts more than not having it.

text: Sell when you can; you are not for all markets.
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 5
plain: Take the offer while it exists. Your value is not for everyone, and it will not last forever.

text:
Twice did he turn his back and purposed so;
But kindness, nobler ever than revenge,
And nature, stronger than his just occasion,
Made him give battle to the lioness,
Who quickly fell before him; in which hurtling
From miserable slumber I awaked.
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 3
plain: He had every reason to walk away from his enemy. Kindness beat revenge.

text:
’Twas I; but ’tis not I. I do not shame
To tell you what I was, since my conversion
So sweetly tastes, being the thing I am.
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 3
plain: You can be ashamed of who you were and still be proud of who you became.

text: Why then, can one desire too much of a good thing?
location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
plain: Even good things can be wanted past the point of sense.

text:
I sometimes do believe and sometimes do not,
As those that fear they hope, and know they fear.
location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Hope and fear arrive together. You can want something so badly you are scared to believe in it.

text: Rich honesty dwells like a miser, sir, in a poor house, as your pearl in your foul oyster.
location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: Something valuable can live in a plain, unimpressive package.

text: He uses his folly like a stalking-horse, and under the presentation of that he shoots his wit.
location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
plain: The sharpest people hide behind looking foolish and strike from there.

text:
I to the world am like a drop of water
That in the ocean seeks another drop,
Who, failing there to find his fellow forth,
Unseen, inquisitive, confounds himself.
So I, to find a mother and a brother,
In quest of them, unhappy, lose myself.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Searching for someone else can make you lose track of yourself.

text:
He that commends me to mine own content
Commends me to the thing I cannot get.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Being told to just be content is advice to go get the one thing you cannot find.

text:
A wretched soul bruis’d with adversity,
We bid be quiet when we hear it cry;
But were we burd’ned with like weight of pain,
As much, or more, we should ourselves complain:
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Telling someone to stay calm is easy when it is not your pain.

text:
When the sun shines let foolish gnats make sport,
But creep in crannies when he hides his beams.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: Fair-weather people show up when things are good and vanish when they are not.

text:
Am I in earth, in heaven, or in hell?
Sleeping or waking, mad, or well-advis’d?
Known unto these, and to myself disguis’d!
I’ll say as they say, and persever so,
And in this mist at all adventures go.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: When nothing makes sense, keep moving and let it clear as you go.

text:
Time is a very bankrupt, and owes more than he’s worth to season.
Nay, he’s a thief too. Have you not heard men say
That time comes stealing on by night and day?
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 4 Scene 2
plain: Time quietly takes everything, and it owes you nothing.

text:
Sweet recreation barr’d, what doth ensue
But moody and dull melancholy,
Kinsman to grim and comfortless despair,
And at her heels a huge infectious troop
Of pale distemperatures and foes to life?
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Cut out rest and play and what follows is gloom, then despair, then sickness.

text:
In food, in sport, and life-preserving rest
To be disturb’d would mad or man or beast.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Take away food, play and sleep and anyone will crack.

text:
O! grief hath chang’d me since you saw me last,
And careful hours with time’s deformed hand,
Have written strange defeatures in my face.
location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
plain: Worry and years change your face until people stop recognizing you.

text:
He that depends
Upon your favours swims with fins of lead,
And hews down oaks with rushes.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Live on other people's approval and you are swimming with weights and chopping trees with reeds.

text:
With every minute you do change a mind
And call him noble that was now your hate,
Him vile that was your garland.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: The crowd flips on you every minute. Their praise and their hate are both weather.

text:
Who deserves greatness
Deserves your hate; and your affections are
A sick man’s appetite, who desires most that
Which would increase his evil.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Anyone great gets hated. And people often crave exactly what makes them worse.

text:
Sir, praise me not.
My work hath yet not warmed me.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 5
plain: Do not clap for me yet. I have barely started.

text:
You shall not be
The grave of your deserving.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 9
plain: Do not bury your own worth by hiding it.

text:
Now put your shields before your hearts, and fight
With hearts more proof than shields.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 4
plain: Armor helps, but a tougher heart is what holds.

text:
He that has but effected his good will
Hath overta’en mine act.
location: Coriolanus, Act 1 Scene 9
plain: Someone who simply did what they meant to do has matched anything I did.
